summary: A JavaScript hack that ensures modal popups and Ajax Toolkit components function correctly in browsers using the WebKit engine (including Chrome and Safari 3), by updating the browser detection logic.
purpose: To resolve compatibility issues with Ajax Toolkit features (such as modal popups) in Chrome and Safari 3 by making them recognizable as WebKit browsers.

workflows.name: WebKit Browser Detection Hack
steps: Check if the user agent string contains 'WebKit/'.
If so, set Sys.Browser.agent to Sys.Browser.WebKit.
Set Sys.Browser.version to the parsed WebKit version from the user agent.
This enables Ajax Toolkit modal popups and other functionality to work correctly.

business_rules: Browser is considered WebKit if the user agent contains 'WebKit/'.
Sys.Browser.WebKit is defined as an empty object to facilitate detection.
validations: User agent string must contain 'WebKit/' to trigger the hack.
calculations: Parse the WebKit version from the user agent using regex: /WebKit\/(\d+(\.\d+)?)/.
system_behavior: Enables Ajax Toolkit modal popups to work in Chrome and Safari 3 by adjusting Sys.Browser properties.
dependencies: Relies on the presence of Sys.Browser and navigator.userAgent.
exceptions: This hack is only applied if 'WebKit/' is found in the user agent; otherwise, no changes are made.
content_gaps: No information on how this impacts non-WebKit browsers.
No details on long-term maintenance or compatibility with newer browser versions.
